applicableAreas: Southern boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Trees shown planted along southern boundary adjacent to overhead electric line cannot be verified as utility-compatible (per ECM Appendix F UC column) because the species of trees near the OHE facility are not identified on the landscape plan. Plant schedule lists all proposed species but does not indicate which species are located at the OHE line. Species identification required to verify compliance with 15-foot non-utility-compatible tree clearance requirement from distribution conductor.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are proposed within 25-foot lateral distance of distribution conductor. Proposed shade trees include Cedar Elm and Live Oak (typically 40-50+ feet mature height), but landscape plan does not differentiate large-maturing trees from smaller species or indicate their specific locations. Without species identification for trees near OHE line, cannot verify compliance with 25-foot clearance requirement for large trees from distribution conductor.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary overhead electric line area
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not identify tree species of trees shown near the overhead electric line on the southern boundary. Landscape plan symbols (e.g., circles with center marks or M for mitigation) lack species labels. Plant schedule (Sheet 35) lists all proposed species and quantities but provides no cross-reference indicating which species are planted at which locations on the landscape plan, particularly for trees near utility facilities. Species identification is required to verify clearance compliance.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan to allow verification of their locations relative to overhead electric facilities. Plant schedule lists Cedar Elm (10 trees, typically 40+ feet mature height) and Live Oak (2 trees, typically 40+ feet mature height) but does not designate them as large trees or indicate their specific planting locations. Cannot verify that large trees are not within 25-foot clearance zone of distribution conductor.

While trees are shown on the landscape plan and the overhead electric line is depicted, clearance verification is prevented due to insufficient documentation. Landscape plan lacks: (1) species identification for trees near the OHE facility, (2) lateral distance dimensions from tree trunks to the overhead conductor, (3) clearance zone markings, (4) differentiation between conductor location and pole centerline. Without these elements, compliance with distribution clearance requirements cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether trees proposed within prohibited clearance zones have documented Austin Energy written approval. Species and measured distances cannot be determined from landscape plan due to lack of species identification and distance dimensions. Electric Review references Austin Energy design criteria requirements (Bluebeam link) but no approval letter or coordination memorandum from Austin Energy authorizing tree placement is included in submitted plans.
